items.q: Explain to a non-engineer why a reverse-osmosis membrane needs pre-treatment.
items.a: RO membranes have extremely fine pores. Without pre-treatment, particles, hardness and chlorine foul, scale or chemically damage them, so output drops and membranes must be replaced early. Filters, softening or antiscalant, and carbon to remove chlorine protect them.
crit: Mentions fouling or clogging by particles
Mentions scaling from hardness or minerals
Uses plain language without heavy jargon

items.q: Give three risks of launching a product without market research, each with one mitigation.
items.a: 1) Nobody wants it - run 10 customer interviews first. 2) Wrong price - test two price points on a landing page. 3) A competitor already owns the niche - do a one-day competitor scan.

items.a: Studies show 94.7% of products fail without research (Harvard 2021). Risk: failure. Mitigation: do research.

items.q: Summarise the trade-off between batch and continuous production in under 80 words.
items.a: Batch production is flexible: you can switch products easily, but changeovers cost time and unit costs are higher. Continuous production runs one product non-stop with low unit cost and steady quality, but it is expensive to set up and hard to change. Choose batch for variety and small volumes, continuous for high, stable demand.
crit: Names flexibility as a batch advantage
Names lower unit cost or efficiency as a continuous advantage
Gives guidance on when to choose which
